To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel protein C-terminal prelylcysteine methyl esterase activity was identified in the cytosol and plasma membrane of brain and other tissues.

(a) the C-terminal prenylcysteine methylation status of the G25K protein is regulated by reversible carboxyl methylesterase activity, (b) this enzyme activity may regulate the cellular distribution and activity of the protein by controlling its prenylcysteinylated and demethylesterified states, (c) the methylesterase is a novel enzyme with unique properties and is likely a distinct protein, and (d) a membrane-associated form of
the C-terminal prenylcysteine methyl ester of G25K is a substrate for a brain enzyme which is a member of a family of carboxyl methyl esterases that are widely distributed in mammalian tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a soluble and membrane-associated protein C-terminal prenylesterase from rabbit brain.
the characterization and purification of a brain methylesterase which hydrolyzes the C-terminal prenylcysteine methylation of the small G-protein, G25K.
the reversible methylation of G25K.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain methylesterase activity is a complex mixture of enzymes with different properties.

there are two different soluble and membrane-associated methylesterase forms of the enzyme, one of which is the physiologically significant form, and the second of which is a proteolytic form of the enzyme.
the methylation of G25K is reversible, and that methylation may be regulated by the methylesterase activity associated with the membrane fraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there exists a protein carboxyl methyl esterase that is capable of cleaving the C-terminal methyl ester of G25K and that this enzyme may be responsible for the methylation of G25K.
the C-terminal geranylated cysteine residue of G25K is a target for reversible carboxyl methylesterification by a brain-specific protein C-terminal prenylesterase.
there is at least one soluble and one membrane associated form of the enzyme in brain, and the soluble form may represent a precursor form of the membrane associated form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal prenylcysteine methylation of G25K is regulated by reversible methylation and demethylation of the Cys residue by a protein carboxylmethylase.
the C-terminal prenylcysteine methyl ester of G25K can be removed in a cell-free system by a specific methylesterase activity that is present in brain homogenates.

the methylation of the G25K C-terminus is a dynamic process and the enzyme responsible for the methylesterification of the G25k C-terminus, protein C-terminal prenlyl-cysteines methylesterase, is present at the plasma membrane.
